Only methods declared in candy-tetris/src, or inherited from a parent declared there, are listed. A type that extends a class outside that tree, such as \RuntimeException, does not show the methods of that class.

Board final class

The 10×20 Tetris playfield (the "well"), plus a 4-row hidden buffer above it where new pieces spawn before they cross into the visible area.

MethodSummary
__construct(?array $cells = null)
isOccupied(int $x, int $y): bool
cellAt(int $x, int $y): ?Tetromino
fits(Piece $piece): boolTrue iff every cell of $piece is in-bounds AND not already occupied. Used both for "can the piece move here" and for "did the new spawn collide on entry" (game-over check).
place(Piece $piece): selfLock $piece into the board, returning a new Board with those cells filled with the piece's Tetromino kind.
clearLines(): arrayClear any rows that are completely full. Returns [newBoard, $clearedCount]. Cleared rows are dropped and empty rows are inserted at the top (hidden buffer end) so everything above falls down.
dropPiece(Piece $piece): PieceDrop $piece straight down until it can't fall any further. Returns the resting position (without locking it in).
rows(): array
isPerfectClear(): boolTrue iff the board is completely empty (all cells null). Used to detect a "perfect clear" — all lines cleared at once.

static startWithLockDelay(?Bag $bag = null, int $lockDelayMs = self::DEFAULT_LOCK_DELAY_MS, ?KeyBindings $bindings = null, ?Scores $scores = null, ?string $scoresPath = null, bool $introPending = false, ?int $seed = null, bool $reproducible = false, ?\Closure $clockUs = null): selfStart a new game with a real-time lock-delay window enabled.
init(): ?\Closure
update(Msg $msg): array
withNotice(string $line): selfcandy-tetris-025/-092: the single push point for the pending-frame slot — never a raw write while the loop owns the terminal. Oldest line gives way; the two freshest ride the next banner.
introBeginLabel(): stringThe key names the on-ramp card prints for the start action (m27: a remapped begin shows remapped on the card). Candy-tetris-053: the frame glyph pair 'spc ent' read as one impossible chord to a new player — the card spells the keycaps ('Space or Enter') and joins them with the locale's own disjunction; a custom remap token that has no display name shows itself verbatim.
keyLabel(string $id): stringThe live, human-readable name of an action's bindings (candy-tetris- 005): every banner that tells the player to press something must print the table as it stands, never a baked literal — a remapped pause whose overlay still says 'p' strands the player at the screen it claims to unlock. Tokens render in keycap long form and join with the locale's own disjunction, so 'q' + 'ctrl+c' reads 'q or ctrl+c'.
view(): string
applyAiMove(int $rotDelta, int $dx): selfApply an AI move in one call: rotate the current piece by $rotDelta times (naive, no kicks), shift it by $dx if that fits, hard-drop it, lock, and spawn the next piece.
addGarbage(int $count, ?\Closure $rand = null): selfReceive garbage the way production does (candy-tetris-026): the VS hot path's entry point. With no explicit $rand the holes ride THIS game's seeded stream — the run's root seed (candy-tetris-018) thus controls the whole match: pieces, holes, everything. An unseeded global default is no longer reachable from any production path; fresh entropy is captured once at launch instead.
addGarbageRows(int $count, ?\Closure $rand = null): selfReceive garbage rows from the opponent: the new rows enter at the BOTTOM and push existing content up (classic Tetris garbage). The active piece rides the lift when there is room; a piece pinned against the ceiling keeps its row, and a piece with neither option (its raised or original cell set collides with locked content) tops the game out. Garbage never destroys locked content silently: if the stack already occupies the ceiling rows the lift would need, the receive is a top-out instead.
subscriptions(): ?\SugarCraft\Core\Subscriptions

GravityMsg final class

Dispatched once per gravity tick — carries the chain generation it was armed under (Game::$gravityChain) and the monotonic deadline (µs, hrtime) the arm asked the loop to fire at (candy-tetris-023); the handler chains the NEXT arm one interval after it, so re-arm timing is measured against virtual schedule, not against the moment processing finally got around to it. A tick whose tag mismatches, or which arrives with no slot taken, is stale and goes inert. The Game's tick handler steps the active piece down one row (or locks it + spawns the next one if it can't move further) and re-arms the chain only while none is pending (Game::$gravityPending), so player actions can never stack ticks. When a lock-delay window owns the timing the handler parks the chain instead of re-arming; the input path revives it. $deadlineUs is null for hand-built test shapes — a null answers "arm a fresh baseline", exactly the pre-deadline behaviour.

MethodSummary
__construct(public readonly int $chain = 0, public readonly ?float $deadlineUs = null)

Renderer final class

Pure view function for Game. Returns the rendered frame string ready to hand to the SugarCraft Renderer.

MethodSummary
static render(Game $game): string
static restartHintLines(Game $game): arrayThe over-screen hint as one or two banner lines (candy-tetris-005): the clause pair is joined in the catalogue by the house em-dash, and the fold re-splits it so a wide remap — or the honest two-token quit — can never be clipped mid-word by the frame width. With the shipped table this renders exactly the two sentences the old single line held, stacked; a locale that stops carrying the joiner simply stays one line (and LocaleParityTest fails the roster first).

Score final class

Score / level / lines tracker. Standard NES Tetris scoring:

MethodSummary
__construct(public readonly int $points = 0, public readonly int $lines = 0, public readonly int $level = 0)
withLines(int $cleared): self
framesPerRow(): intFrames-per-row gravity at the current level. Cribbed from NES Tetris: starts at 48 frames/row at level 0, steps down through 2 frames/row for levels 19-28, and holds at 1 frame/row from level 29 up. We're frame-rate-agnostic (SugarCraft uses a wall-clock tick), so consumers convert this to a microsecond delay via framesPerRow() * 16667 (i.e. 60 fps).
gravityIntervalUs(): intMicroseconds to wait between gravity steps.
withDropPoints(int $points): selfAdd points from a hard-drop or soft-drop. Lines and level are unchanged (unlike withLines() which may level up).

SugarCraft\Tetris\Support

Bindings final class

MethodSummary
static mapIds(): arrayThe dispatch ids (candy-tetris-015's completeness pin reads them).
static table(): KeyBindings
static actuates(KeyBindings $keys, KeyMsg $msg, string $id): boolApp-side actuation door (candy-tetris-034): under a ctrl chord only 'ctrl+…' tokens of the action actuate; without one only plain tokens do. The sugar-core registry once folded modifiers away, so Ctrl+C answered the plain 'c' token and actuated HOLD mid-drop instead of leaving. Its matches() is now chord-exact, which already gives this split, and also stops a bare token firing under Alt or Shift (Alt+c no longer holds, Shift+Space no longer hard-drops); the ctrl leg stays as a pin of the contract. Releases and repeats never actuate (m11), on either leg.
static isKnownToken(string $token): boolThe key-name vocabulary for config validation (candy-tetris-032): a single printable character (the decoder emits runes lowercased, and a space arrives as the 'space' name), any named key the decoder can emit, or a 'ctrl+' chord over either. A typo like 'spce' is NOT a key any stream can actuate — loading it "valid" is how begin got stranded behind undismissable intro cards (UXD-05). Case is folded the way KeyBindings folds override tokens.
static helpCard(KeyBindings $bindings): stringThe single-player help card, derived from the live bindings.
static vsStrip(KeyBindings $bindings): stringThe versus-mode key strip — the SAME live rows and verbs as the solo card, chunked three to a line so the full table fits the width-50 match strip (candy-tetris-015: five of eleven was not teaching).
static verbColumn(): arrayThe translated verb column — fail-loud on shape (candy-tetris-077: the old ?? '' legs rendered a blank verb when a locale lost a line, so a missing binding name became invisible instead of a bug).
static verbColumnFrom(string $cardText): arrayThe parse door self::verbColumn() routes the live catalogue through — public as the test seam for the fail-loud arm (a suite cannot fake a broken shipped file, but it can name the contract on a truncated column).

Paint final class

MethodSummary
static banner(string $body, array $lines): stringReplace the vertically-centred band of full-width rows through the body with the given plain-text lines, each centred across that width. The frame's row and column counts NEVER change — an overlay is a stripe across the playfield, not content appended past the fold (the C-2 below-the-bend defect this posture cured).
static refusal(): stringPlain-text refusal for a terminal with no rendering capability at all (MA-12): zero SGR bytes, nothing to misparse. The floor is the TTY itself — colour is optional (NO_COLOR/CLICOLOR=0 play fine), so the copy must not demand colour (candy-tetris-041); one line now answers for both modes (candy-tetris-027).
static tooSmallNotice(string $key, int $minCols, int $minRows, int $cols, int $rows): stringNotice shown below the frame floor; wrapped to the ACTUAL terminal width (candy-tetris-024: the old max(20, cols) let the very notice explaining that the frame won't fit overflow a narrower terminal, clipping mid-word). A word longer than the width is emitted on its own line and clips by character — the notice staying on-screen matters more than the notice staying whole.
static wrap(string $text, int $width): stringGreedy word wrap of plain text honouring existing newlines. A word wider than the whole width is hard-split by codepoints (width-aware: an east-asian cell consumes two) — below 20 columns the notice's longest words outgrow the terminal, and a wrap that lets them through re-creates the clip it exists to cure (candy-tetris-024).
static cellMap(array $cells): arrayOccupancy lookup for a piece cell list, keyed "x,y".

Scores final class

MethodSummary
__construct(public readonly ?int $soloBest = null, public readonly int $soloGames = 0, public readonly int $versusWins = 0, public readonly int $versusLosses = 0, public readonly bool $onboarded = false, private readonly ?self $baseline = null)
static load(?string $path): ?selfRead the record at $path. Null means "nothing to read": no path was resolvable, or the file does not exist yet. Corruption — and any non-regular occupant of the slot — throws; the caller decides how loudly to be.
save(string $path): selfWrite the record atomically at 0600 (mode settled before the publish rename), merged with whatever the file holds NOW (candy-tetris-035): the disk is re-read, this session's deltas since its boot anchor are applied on top, and the best becomes the max of both views. A file that became unreadable mid-run falls back to the legacy straight write — the launcher already refused to boot from it, and losing the current session's own settlement would be the louder failure.
withSolo(int $points): selfSettle one finished solo game: the best never moves backwards and the games counter walks by exactly one.
beatsSoloBest(int $points): boolTrue when $points beats every solo game settled so far.
withVersusResult(bool $playerWon): selfRecord one finished versus match from the local player's seat.

Version final class

The version string this tool reports on --version.

MethodSummary
static line(): stringThe --version line: plain text, newline-terminated, produced by no state and no host probe — the flag must answer anywhere.
static current(): stringThe version this process reports: the archive stamp when running from a stamped phar, self::CURRENT everywhere else.
static fromPharMetadata(string $path): ?stringThe version a phar archive at $path was built to carry, or null when it names none (unreadable archive, wrong metadata shape, the dev-build sentinel, or an empty stamp). Every refusal is a null, never an exception — --version must answer on a machine whose phar cannot be opened.
static versionFromMetadata(mixed $metadata): ?stringThe judgement on the stamp itself, split out because the archive-open leg is unreachable from a suite that must not build phars: the release namespace strip, the dev-build refusal, and the wrong-type nulls are a pure function over what getMetadata() answers.
static hostArchive(): stringThe filesystem path of the phar this process was launched from, or '' when it was not launched from one — the two-identity law measured on candy-code's real builds and pinned by the bin autoload guard: inside archive-loaded code Phar::running(false) answers the archive path, while the stub context answers '' and there a '.phar'-suffixed __DIR__ is the enclosing archive.
